subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class cron output targets, and what rules should govern file writes, channel fan-out, session injection, silent discard, fallback, and run-status reporting?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix creates new framework-owned file, channel, and cross-session delivery authority that automation should not define without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design one output contract
options.body: Define a single cron output target API with explicit authorization, path policy, delivery semantics, docs, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to delivery defaults
options.body: Defer file and session targets and solve only the focused default-recipient problem tracked by the related delivery-default issue.

options.title: Reject core output targets
options.body: Keep cron routing prompt/tool-driven or plugin-owned and improve diagnostics/docs instead of adding new core delivery authority.

recommendation.title: Design one output contract
recommendation.body: Define a single cron output target API with explicit authorization, path policy, delivery semantics, docs, and regression tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron delivery/docs and is already connected to this issue discussion.
